'''Slava Epstein''' is an American academic of [[Soviet Jewish|Soviet-Jewish]] origin, researcher and entrepreneur working in the field of [[Microbial ecology]]. He is currently a professor in the biology department of [[Northeastern University]] and co-founder of [[NovoBiotic Pharmaceuticals]].  As a researcher his most covered contribution is the development of the [[Isolation chip]] (iChip) and the discovery of a new antibiotic, [[Teixobactin]]. Epstein's research has been published in many leading scientific journals including ''Nature'' and ''Science''.

== Early life ==
Slava Epstein was born in the Soviet Union in a Jewish family.  As a kid he was fascinated with astronomy and dreamed of being a physicist, however due to strict Soviet anti-semitic quotas he was advised to switch to biology.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=The Dark Matter - from space to biology and back {{!}} Slava Epstein {{!}} TEDxBratislava|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NIjFtTQzrrE|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=[[YouTube]]}}</ref>  

== Education ==

Slava Epstein received an M.S. in marine biology from [[Moscow State University]] in 1981 and PhD in microbial ecology from the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]], Shirshov Institute of Oceanology in 1986.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Slava Epstein|url=https://www.northeastern.edu/graduate/bio/slava-epstein/|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=}}</ref> For his research he traveled to the [[White Sea]] to study protozoan organisms.<ref>{{Cite magazine|last=|first=|date=|title=Miracle Microbes|url=https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2016/06/20/miracle-microbes|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|magazine=[[The New Yorker]]}}</ref>

== Immigration to the United States ==
Epstein immigrated with his family from the [[Soviet Union]] in late 1980's.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Indiana Jones- style professor explores frontiers of microbial science.|url=https://news.northeastern.edu/2009/02/03/slava-epstein/|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=}}</ref> He first volunteered, then completed a postdoc at the [[University of Massachusetts, Boston]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=A radically simple idea may open the door to a new world of antibiotics.|url=https://www.statnews.com/2015/12/03/antibiotics-bacteria-research/|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=}}</ref> Since 1992, he has worked at Northeastern University, where he is a professor in the biology department. <ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Slava Epstein|url=https://www.northeastern.edu/graduate/bio/slava-epstein/|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=}}</ref>

== Career ==
His main field of research is microbial ecology along with cultivation and discovery of previously unculturable microorganisms.  Along with Kim Lewis, he is credited with development of the Isolation Chip (iChip).<ref>{{Cite journal|date=2010|title=Use of ichip for high-throughput in situ cultivation of "uncultivable" microbial species|url=https://aem.asm.org/content/76/8/2445|journal=Applied and Environmental Microbiology|volume=Apr 2010|pages=76 (8) 2445-2450|bibcode=2010ApEnM..76.2445N|via=|last1=Nichols|first1=D.|last2=Cahoon|first2=N.|last3=Trakhtenberg|first3=E. S.|issue=8|doi=10.1128/AEM.01754-09|pmid=20173072|pmc=2849220}}</ref> He was on the team along with Kim Lewis that discovered a previously unknown antibiotic [[Teixobactin]], by screening soil bacteria using novel cultivation methods, particularly by cultivating the ''[[Eleftheria terrae]],'' the antibiotic-producing bacteria in soil, which is the organism's natural environment.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=A new antibiotic kills pathogens without detectable resistance|journal=Nature|year=2015|volume=517|pages=455 − 459 (2015)|doi=10.1038/nature14098|pmid=25561178|last1=Ling|first1=L. == Awards and honors ==
Foreign Policy Magazine Leading Global Thinkers 2015, along with [[Kim Lewis (academic)|Kim Lewis]].  For the discovery of antibiotic Taixobactin in a pile of dirt.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=FP Leading Global Thinkers 2015, Healers|url=https://2015globalthinkers.foreignpolicy.com/#!healers/list|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=}}</ref>
